FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 8 May 1968, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseed. Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 India is an important cotton producing country, producing about 2 million tonnes of cottonseed as a by-product of the cotton industry, which can yield about 250 000 tonnes of good oil. Large quantities of cottonseed went for cattle feeding. During the last ten years, Government has taken several steps to encourage cottonseed crushing with the active assistance of the VA.NASP.4TI industry in providing a ready market for cottonseed oil. 0.2.1 The major cottonseed producing areas in the country are, Maharastra, Punjab, Mysore, Madhya Pradesh, Madras, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh. The two types of cottonseeds popularly grown in India are (a) American (fuzzy) type, and (b) D,s; (nonfuzzy) type. The former type contains lints about 5 to 12 percent and latter averaging S percent.

0.3 The specification for the oil obtained Crom cottonseed is covered by
IS : 543-1963� and IS : 3472-1966t.

0.4 This standard contains clause 5.1 which calls for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 0.5 For the pur~e of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or anatyail, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960:. The number of significant place. retained in the rounded off value should be the lame as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE l.t Thil ltandard prescribes the methods or sradiDl and the r~uire. ments for cottonseeCk for oil mUting along with the relevant methOds or sampling and telt.
2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard definitions given under 2 of IS : 3579-1966� shall apply.
3. GRADES

3.1 The material shall be of three grades, namely, Grade 1, Grade 2 and Grade 3.

4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Descriptio. - The material shall be obtained from the plants of Goslypium species belonging to family Malvaceae. 4.2 The material shall be clean and free from oilseed. other than cottonseeds (see 4.2.1). The material shall also be free from argemone and castor seeds and husk and other non-edibleoilseeds � 4.1.1 Presence of Salmalia malabarica Schott and Endl. 8yo. Bombax malabaricum and Celba penlandr" ( Linn. ) Gaertn. syn, Eriodendron anfractuosum DC (silk cotton) seeds shall be taken as adulterant impurities. 4.3 The material shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1.
5. PACKING S.1 The material shall be supplied in clean, dry and sound lingle new or unmended B-Twill bagl in merchantable condition al agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
,. MARKING

6.1 The bagl shall be marked with the name, grade and weight cottonseeds, the year of crop and the source of supply. 7. SAMPUNG

of the
